reviews.text: I'm not a MOBA player (even if it's more of a blend of MOBA/hack’n’slash/tower def/roguelite/RTS) and I don’t totally get everything I’m doing, but it’s super fun. I click on stuff, I kill stuff, I loot money after killing those things, I build towers, upgrade my village, kill more stuff, survive hordes of things, fight a boss, die, respawn, get stronger, kill even more stuff, protect my village, collect more and more stuff, wow damn I get way stronger, I feel good so I go back to kill the boss. I take him down after a long fight and get tons of stuff to upgrade even more stuff. Lots of stuff killed, lots of fun. Me like. Game good.

开发商是傻逼？单人游戏网络波动一下都能给我踢出游戏？而且局内还没有一丁点的保存系统，被踢出来就当我白玩了？ 更逆天的是断网开始游戏，连上网络以后也会自动进入多人游戏然后给我从单人游戏里面踢出来？？？？？？ 更不提偶尔出现的卡顿，闪退环节。 你局外设置的这么肝，单人游戏跟联机游戏体验还巨差，还不如demo版本，我都不知道你们怎么做的游戏？ 2026年3月28日凌晨2点编辑 开发商修复问题挺快的，联机卡顿好一点了，单人虽然目前没试但是应该没有什么问题（有问题就又来改评论了）。 就是联机模式什么时候调整一下，科技没办法带到别人那里用还好说，为什么战具跟精粹升级都没办法带到别人那里用啊。 这联机纯粹就是进别人那里打工，要不你进度推得飞快让别人复制你存档逃离牢房，要不就是你进别人那里从零开始坐牢。 这也太极端了吧，新朋友来玩的话，去他那里玩强行从零开始玩起来，为什么不能用高等级的战具与精粹进去带人！！

Finally get to play DOTA without having to deal with DOTA players. Feels very much like Warcraft 3 & StarCraft 2 custom maps, but with a lot more "just one more game" feeling. The maps and runs vary enough that it isn't just following a preset build every game (or trying something new and having your teammates yell at you). It does have the classic MOBA experience of dozens of small mechanics poorly explained that actually have a massive impact (upgrading Recruitment buildings/towns is huge - synergizing Boons as well) - but is addicting once you get it down. I received a free test version before release and have only played single player which has run fine but with a high end machine - feels like a complete game for a reasonable price. BUT apparently co-op has some pretty serious issues with progression and design, so if you actually have friends you may want to recosider.

This is a game I want to recommend but I don't think I can. First, it's a game that requires a lot of dedication of time. 30-60min for a run with no ability to save mid game. It's like this because the target audience is MOBA gamers used to LoL or DoTA and is very much tailored toward the co-op side of things. Except that it doesn't have the depth and complexity in gameplay or interesting characters those games have, and so leaves a lot to be desired game to game. Couple this with the excessively grindy nature of the game and you end up feeling like you've wasted a lot of time when you don't win. This is all made worse by the fact that the game punishes you really hard for exploring and not playing optimally by scaling the lanes WAY to fast. Look, if I want to spend 8 hours on a map trying to 100% it without dying to see all there is on offer, fking LET ME ENJOY THE WORK YOU PUT INTO THE GAME! Lastly, I've tried to play 6 games as of this writing and the game crashed in three of them. Two of them 30min+ in, usually while in a dungeon. With no way to recover and no progress made, it really was just a waste of time. There is a HUGE amount of potential here and I want more games like this to be made that take the MOBA gameplay style and apply it to different genres. Ridiculous reasons to be in a situations with multiple lanes of endlessly spawning mobs has a lot of potential for mindless fun. This doesn't quite hit the mark though. My biggest gripes: - The customization is overly random preventing builds to work toward. You either get lucky and get what you need when you need it or lose. Alternatively grind the game until you unlock the ability to start with a build. - Enemies are WAY too durable. Maybe after making some progress it would be fine but enemies go from 400hp with 15 or so enemies in a wave to 1100 after 15min or so. Meanwhile your auto-attack does 60 damage and only scales if you find random upgrades that give you 3-6 more damage. - Your own mobs do not scale the same as your opponent. I'm not even sure your units scale at all? Imagine having a mechanic where capturing certain areas gives you access to lane upgrades and taking areas from your opponent weakens them given the chance to push. - It's very repetitive all things considered since the difficulty is tied to health and damage stats instead of mechanics that make it more fun. More challenge is added through more and more handicaps, but nothing changes for the player. Despite not unlocking all the characters yet, it already feels like I've found everyway to play already. - Lastly, there's no personality in any of the characters. You get a few abilities to make the characters unique with a bunch of abilities that cause them to feel the same. Everyone has their way to avoid damage, a "strike" ability, then they get the abilities you give them, which take a long time to unlock so you end up getting stuck playing the same repetitive games.

Look. I understand the official Steam policy is that 2 hours is the maximum playtime for a game to be refundable. But I humbly requested that they allow me to refund this. I was ASTOUNDED to find out so many multiplayer issues that make the game just... unbearable. First of all, there is no matchmaking. So at first I think, no biggie, I'll just try to play solo since that's a marketing bullet-point. One map length is about 1 hour long. And I'm marginally okay with the game, it's pretty good, so I try it again. Struggle through, and fail about halfway. I put the game down for a few days, I think, and go back in. Notice there's a Discord button and hop into one of their "LOOK FOR GROUP" voice chats. Link up with a guy, pretty effortlessly... using their "Lobby Code" system sorta like SpaceMarine2. But therein lies the first and honestly, biggest problem. You can't just hit a button and join a queue and be randomly matched up with .... whoever. You have to either KNOW two other people who own the game, or join THEIR discord server... Now the other thing that was the straw that broke the camels back was that not only was I more or less forced to join another guy's lobby -- The progress in that lobby is TIED TO HIS ACCOUNT -- NOT MINE. So I am 4 "game's" into playing, again, one map is approx 1 hour long maximum, and we finish this fourth game and I see that we've unlocked a whole lot of unlockable currency... So I spend it -- thinking I was upgrading MY character. No! I just spent 5000 whatever coins in THAT guys game -- completely unknowingly. I apologized profusely to the guy and said look this game is fun and all but this is just ..... unreal. I thanked him for showing me how to play the game as a group but I was so sorry I just blew a bunch of his currency. But again, if I spend however long playing in his lobby, upgrading his character, or even his lobby so to speak, with higher difficulties and whatnot, Then If someone else joins MY lobby we go back to being level 1 again and it's like ... dude I can play this game indefinitely in other players lobbies and I can effectively get absolutely nowhere in this game. WHY would I keep this?

游戏整体框架还行，但是部分设定还是有点过于沉积在自我艺术里，无法让人不去吐吐槽。 画面，设定都可以，但是核心成长系统和敌方DBUFF系统太稀烂。烂到可以堪称俄罗斯套娃一般组合拳！！！ 第一层大套娃：局外成长杯水车薪，先说英雄，局外的英雄属性那边看似给了不少，什么伤害/CD/hp/经验+50%，但是也就仅此而已。英雄的基本三围是不会变的，随着过关难度高了以后基础属性根本不跟不上难度曲线。（与随后的DUFF系统深度套娃）英雄虽然说是可以升级4个阶级，但阶级的作用除了给开自选被动以外就是一坨。但凡你每点一次都加点英雄三围都不至于这么憨逼。 第二层大套娃，局内的升级就纯属搞笑，都说这个梦回魔兽守护雅典娜，但是人家好歹升级能正常加点属性，你这倒好，那是一点都不给。核心的四种碎片属性，但是鉴于肉鸽底层逻辑，运气差点出门全是你对不上号的属性碎片。（BOSS：喜不喜欢我开局第一夜2K血的杂鱼骷髅海但你普攻只有60，主属性宝石不过0的膀胱局啊！） 第三层大套娃，我方建筑与兵力，总体来说随着世界等级提升，局外即使点满了也是杯水车薪。兵力虽然+6，但在后期敌方加成算法下，我方兵线推不动。经济建筑虽然看似加钱很多，但前提是你要修的起来（经济系统也是套娃之一，而且和惩罚系统相加更是粪中粪）三种塔总共只能修6个还时不时给你封印一天一个。 第四层大套娃，独特（粪作）的惩罚系统，随时空等级的增加，常驻开局200%血攻杂鱼，一天250%的加攻，最大10次天气变化，5个锻造蠕虫都是小事，但是偏偏里面混了个限时死亡300s等级+1这个爹！甚至他们还贴心的给你安排了和蔼可亲的巡逻队天天断你经济！！！！！！！其次再混最多20个神奇因子，那酸爽简直了（开局扣钱，369级解锁技能，白天时间-30s，威能消耗加倍，泉眼枯竭，能量损失等） 第五层大套娃：虽然亲切的设置了花钱能刷新因子和boss，但是TMD要花钱！TMD要花钱！TMD要花钱！还是TMD随纪元递加100！！！！虽然局外点满了那钱无所谓，但是你要是没点满呢！！且额 因子虽然可以降级，你看似前面有个点以为可以自己选，但是其实不能，只能看系统排序心情。 第六层大套娃，现有6英雄，个人觉得狗哥对单输出最高，又有位移，但太脆，纯纯的手累患者，狮爷带线保姆，造型就把答案甩你脸上了，牛哥比较综合但平庸，鹰爷是个弓箭手但也只是个弓箭手罢了，鹿爷攻速和距离都不错但是不太出众，象宝基伤最高，但也仅限如此（你若问我推荐：担1狗2师3牛，其余全是玩具总动员） 第七层大套娃，地图以及任务。总的来说一人太大，两人正好，三人略显拥挤。一人情况下再高纪元难度下就属于哪头都顾不上，四处救火，救着救着就第一天夜来咯，你还什么都没完成甚至于入夜还是卡着惩罚来的（属性也不对，血也没多少，药瓶也没找到合用的 最后的套娃包装盒：你要有至少一个陪你一起品尝“仙味”的好基友！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！ 以上，套娃框架搭好了，接下来请各位看官试想下单人常见套娃：以纪元15为例，起手8次天气突变+200s死亡惩罚+150%的初始杂兵，然后因子开局扣钱导致兜里只有200金，白天时间-30S，369解锁技能，能量损失+神威翻倍，泉水枯竭+家门口泉水经验树被拔了+升级不回复，矿工重生时间翻倍+精英巡逻刷你金矿路上一锤一个小矿工，基地右边开局初见全是弓箭手，左边初见两只大蜘蛛满地爬。好不容易你顺风顺水没什么损失的捡了三个碎片，结果全是裸加你用不上的属性点，第一个神威祭好不容易刷到你 要的属性，但你HP空了，正巧你又没找到野外泉水，好不容易起了一对防御塔修了墙，结果老登上来给你大菠萝附体骨牢一套，墙没了，好巧不巧你入夜还顶着惩罚+2！以上，勇敢的梭（缩）者快去创造奇迹吧！！ 基本吐完，你弱问我推荐不，你如果有能陪你品“仙味”的好基友，那你可以等打折力度大一点入，原价略显稍贵。2黑或者3黑才可以耍，全解锁后就可以丢一边等更新，目前的体积来说，地图太单一，局外成长杯水车薪，局内坐牢太曼巴。 建议在后续更新中修改一下英雄与我方兵力的基础属性成长，好歹能让英雄每升阶一次涨一点基础属性，兵营点一级不光+数量，基础属性也要增加。 PS：不推荐是暂时，等基本改进后再改好评

以我单人20全通关来说，前面5.6关属于技能正常数值能过的关卡，也最好玩，中间5.6关用天赋召唤弓箭手过关也行，后面7.8关，有也只有一个套路，那就是火加流血速推boss ，人物拿弓手，精华拿暗和火，技能拿3个暗技能，那个往返冲是伤害最高CD最短的技能了，天赋拿流血和奔跑不退出隐身，再就是移速，建筑开局点狗和坐骑，再点法师塔减100速度，开局选政令一定要刷10000防护门的血，或者50%金钱造塔，或者每天刷新护盾，局外成长不点满，后面几关过不去，削弱那个加50起始资金的一定刷掉 ，不然最后3关防护门不能架起来第一波就G，然开局就骑狗去搜资源，主选力量，次选攻速射程，每波怪尽量吃到经验，升到6级有2.30力量直接去刷守门boss，运气好拿到加力量的，有了4.50力量或者攻速起来了，守门boss打完，进攻挡一波直接推主，越后面越守不住，钱除了升一级狗和一级法师塔，其他全部用来升级石头塔，不然守不住。套路掌握，后面几关难度基本一样！都是一波带走守门boss和最终boss！都靠远程英雄流血打伤害！反正这游戏数值用脚填的，就前几关还有点技能配合！

This game has a lot of potential. it has a good system of power with a few nit pick blunders but it's very addicting to gain that power. the characters (wargears) to choose from are fun and unique. Since it's PVE it feels more RTS and less moba. For the price it's a worth while game. part of the power system that feels really nice is the shard system/ alter of power. you have 4 types amplifiers: rage, arcane, tactical, fate. you can raise these amplifiers by picking up shards (at creature camps) or at alters of powers by sacrificing your current health. some skills and so evolutions are amplified by these which really gives it that build defining edge. Now the nit picking: the roguelite elements don't feel so great since it's a lot of the same stuff. you will have a pool of 30 none unique character upgrades (common upgrades). 12 or 15 essence upgrades (passives and skills each get 3 options) and only 9 unique character skill upgrades. that totals 53 upgrades total. the main issue with this is that some of these are really defining for a build while others are lack luster. the pot being a mix of everything makes it often feel a lot of the same choices being picked since again it's all in 1 pot and no reason to pick the lesser options unless shafted on options. what amplifiers you are picking end up having more impact then the leveling system itself. As a solo player i feel like the game play loop is repetitive but meanwhile i keep playing other wargears this hasn't bored me yet but im dding a not Developers if you read this. it would be nice to have a more clear indication on the map of what domains, mines or towers still need to be upgraded. you can bring it up in the bastion menu under kingdoms but it adds a step. since the information is already available it would be nice to just see the same tick indicators on the icons in the map menu. also while you are at it can you make escape key close down menus and map. it's a quality of life that is in most games that is hard to unlearn over all great game if you change nothing and run away with my money i wouldn't be upset since i got a lot of worth for it's price for me.

[h1]罕见的支持单人游玩的MOBA[/h1] 即便是在游戏类型百花齐放的2026年，PC端的《英雄联盟》、《DOTA2》，手机端的《王者荣耀》等MOBA类游戏依然大放异彩，占据重要的市场份额。但无疑这些游戏的社交属性都比较强，市面上却鲜少有可以单人游玩的MOBA。而《永恒围城：无尽纪元》这款类MOBA的游戏，除了可以最多3人在线合作游玩外，它同时也支持单人挑战。 之所以说是类MOBA，其实是为了更方便玩家理解这是一个以操控英雄为主，在有着迷雾的地图中战斗的游戏。实际上本作在本质上更像是远古时期的“魔兽RPG地图”。2000年初到2010年左右，当时由于War3强大的地图编辑器和一众才华横溢的地图作者，其在网吧的热度丝毫不低于War3对战本身，甚至造就了各种“XX对战平台”这一特殊历史时期的辉煌产物（现在想起来，还能感受到那种没开VIP就挤不进房间的痛）。 具体来说说本作，故事背景大概就是在某个时空，人类再次迎来了末日，而“堡垒”是最好的希望。为了加固这种堡垒，时间魔法守护者施展咒术展开时光圣域（类似于一种结界）。但是逐渐的，结界开始变得虚弱而不稳定，于是乎我们的各路英雄被征召而来守护堡垒，对抗名为“解织者”的暗黑军团。 游戏的核心玩法就是野外探索养成、基地建设以及战斗。先来说说最核心的战斗，英雄的操控可以采用多种方式，例如传统的MOBA模式或是WASD移动等等，而且支持改键，基本上随心所欲。但是不支持手柄，估计适配有些难度。英雄的普攻为进入攻击范围后自动攻击，但在奔跑时无法攻击，需要切换成步行。在兵营相关建设后，英雄还可以带领小兵一起出征（虽然他们其实并没有太大的作用）。然后英雄可以消耗能量释放不同的技能，技能有各自的属性定位，直观的根据颜色的差异受一种名为“增幅器”的机制影响数据。角色在升级进化时，很多的进化方向就有相应增幅器的加持。总的来说，初始攻击和技能可以视为一个非常基础款的白板，有着大量的升级方向和数值属性的提升。 而在地图方面，存在迷雾，任务目标会有指引。最值得一提的是场景中有着大量的“碎片点”，有怪物守护，打败他们就可以吞噬碎片获得角色各种属性或是增幅器等之类的收益。用更通俗易懂的话来说，这些其实就是打野点。 此外还有金矿之类的资源建筑、各种提高临时增益的圣坛、宝箱神器点以及传送门等设施。甚至还有单独的杀怪副本可以进入，消灭全部怪物后可以组织敌方单位等级的提高。要知道夜晚袭来的解织者人数众多，即便我们也有小兵和防御塔，但单人的话其实也还是蛮棘手的。当然胜利的方法也很简单，在保证己方大本营稳固的前提下适时进行反攻，消灭BOSS就行了。 不过问题也是有的，典型的是游戏目前单人的情况下难度不小，发育期会非常漫长，而且期间能不能防守住也是一个问题。一局搞个1来个小时也是非常正常的，而且我不清楚到底能不能中途保存存档（因为不敢试啊）...局外各种精粹的成长、战具的解锁升级、纪元的成长之路也比较肝，还是需要投入比较大的精力才能逐渐爽起来。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

这游戏我已经满扭曲因子的情况下，打到20纪元了。先说结论，制作者大概率是没玩过这游戏后面的难度的，这数值跟用脚做得没区别，制作组自己也没有去测试过通关难度。对面的数值是2的指数增长的，我方的兵需要去特意激活的，才是0.5的增长和数量上的增长，从头到尾数值都是没有变化的。点名尊者树人，从头到尾都是2400血，这血量单体后期都是直接送的。打到后期我方的士兵几百血打对面上万的血，兵线基本带不出去，而且那个投石车经常冲到最前面然后转身打后面的敌人，我是没想不懂为什么要这样设计。难度方面也是做得一坨，小怪的清理难度比BOSS还要难。光靠兵没有办法防守，梭者要参与防守，而且是要费很多时间，地图的元素很多都没时间去体验，就被迫去通关，拖到后期只会被推家。游戏上其他设计也是意义不明，时光圣殿可以通过牺牲一名梭者换取对面等级一次不增长，一天大概是7分钟左右，梭者死亡对面等级马上增长，并且高难度的持续时间是4分多钟，我花费400金币，提前让对面等级上涨1级4分多钟，换取7分钟后对面的等级保持我现在的在打的等级一样，还有元素方面的设计，全程打下来没有什么帮助。

说起咱们90后00后童年玩过的游戏，《魔兽争霸3》肯定是最具有代表的几款PC游戏之一。说来也巧，我是在搜索“低配电脑能玩什么游戏”时才接触到的War3，不仅游戏本体极为优秀耐玩，玩家社群间对于RPG地图的开发，直接将魔兽的可玩性挖掘到了极致，这种友好分享的互联网精神，才让魔兽成为那个时代的记忆。 今天要介绍的游戏——永恒围城：无尽纪元，想必玩过守卫剑阁/神之墓地等RPG地图的朋友应该很眼熟，守住主城的同时提升自己，逆水行舟不进则退，一旦自己的成长跟不上敌方数值，这局也就失去了胜利的可能性。始终快对面一步，才能将主动权掌握在手中。 游戏里，我们的目标始终只有一个——消灭地图最上方的关底Boss。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3716925419 带有RPG要素的游戏相信不少人玩过，人物养成是最核心的内容之一，完全放弃养成就打boss的成功率趋近为零。 本作也同样如此，到处“练级”无疑是优先级最高的事情。需要注意，在那些有着不小提升“碎片”资源点附近，常常会安排野怪看守，奖励越好的碎片，也意味着更强大的怪物驻守。当然，打野只是探索的一部分，像是“地下城”和“精英Boss”这些高危地点，适合养成一定数值后再去尝试，巨大风险下所带来的回报也是喜人的。 随着我们不断掠夺地图上的资源点，被“战争迷雾”笼罩的地图也将逐渐显现。 提升“梭者”（操控英雄）等级带来的收益最为直观，除了梭者自带的3个技能，想使用局外携带的 “远古精粹”技能，前置条件需到达一定等级，就像是英雄联盟中的召唤师技能，单独占据两个技能栏位。我们可以在战前，根据想玩的英雄搭配技能，是选择梭哈输出追求效率，还是召唤打手当个远程输出的安逸奶妈，都是可以选择的玩法，这一点上比较自由。 除了通过基础人物属性拉高输出，直接选择提升技能伤害，也是一种好方法。但只有选择名为“增幅器”的属性加成，才可增加对应伤害，具体可以在技能上方的标志来判断什么增幅器对此技能生效。如果所有技能同属一种增幅，不能说是最强的组合，但肯定是最省力的组合。要知道，地图中资源有限，无法供给多种属性全面成长，因此需要有一定的取舍。 对于我这种喜欢收集齐地图上大部分资源后，才选择进攻的“慎勇”型玩家，游戏给出的解法是随时间粗暴拉高怪物强度，且可成长性远远大于玩家！所以，并不适合每局都追求全图收集，高难轮回下小怪将会是比Boss更为难缠的对象，推荐清图2/3左右就可以准备去斩杀boss，这时候玩家自身属性也有了一战之力，可以绕过小怪发起斩首行动。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3716925290 游戏设计了一套昼夜交替系统，侧面划分出了玩家行动时间。白天是练级做任务的黄金时间，这时候只会有少量怪物攻城，在友军的防守下完全可以不回家继续探索。 但随着夜晚降临，将不止一波的敌人前来攻城，只要还敢在外面浪荡，分分钟被平推到家门口。这时候招募友军与建造炮塔就派上了用场，活成了塔防游戏的形状。塔防的精髓就是延缓对面的行进速度，有了足够的拉扯空间，面临的防守压力也会大减。 除此之外，合理运营局内的经济系统，直接影响到最后的胜利。金币的主要来源是挖矿和击杀敌人（似乎更像魔兽了？），我们可以拿着钱去建造兵营、铁匠铺等基建设施，主城建造的兵营越多，刷出来的友军也越多，进攻防守都会更加有利。 需要注意的是，道中的炮塔也必须要花钱建造，当一个路口同时拥有两座炮台，就会生成出一道拦截敌人的屏障，有了这些防御设施才能在白天出去安心乱逛。 如果有几个朋友一起开黑那就更好了，这类PVE游戏天然适合开联机，多人分工下可以玩更轻松。本作中梭者并没有传统意义上的职业分类，人人都可以是输出，也都可以当奶妈辅助。 既然说完了游戏的特色，各种影响体验的瑕疵也得展开谈谈。首先就是极其糟糕的平A手感，远程角色尚在我的接受范围内，可一切换到近战角色，极长的出手前摇让每一次走A都相当难受，经常会因为没有对上节奏而卡掉平A，所以当务之急就是好好打磨下手感，普攻作为最使用率最高的输出手段，直接影响整场游戏的体验，是不得不重视的问题。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3716925354 难度曲线不合理也是问题之一。随着难度上升，玩家能获得的正反馈越来越少，每次清理比boss还肉的小怪都是痛苦的体验。而且游戏中的地图池极为稀少，非常容易腻，局外成长也单纯以数值为主，很难持续给玩家来带新鲜感。本作的底子不错，就是缺少了持续带来的爽感，后期巨大的压力时常让玩家应接不暇，是一款优缺点同样明显的作品。 The gameplay itself scratches an itch that I didn't realize I was missing. If you've ever enjoyed jungling in a MOBA, or MOBAs in general, but you're tired of the toxic communities, endless sweating, and teammates flaming each other, this game is a fantastic alternative. It captures that satisfying feeling of clearing camps, growing stronger, and working together without all the stress that usually comes with the genre. For me personally, this has become my "I want a MOBA, but I don't want the headache" game. I'll think about queuing up for a game of Conquest in Smite, remember the disconnects, AFKs, and frustration that have become way too common, and then just boot up Ever Siege instead. I still get that progression and action I'm looking for, but in a much more relaxed environment where I can just have fun. I wouldn't say this game had the smoothest launch. There were a lot of features that honestly should have been there on day one that either weren't implemented yet or weren't even being beta tested. One of the biggest examples was progression while playing with friends. If you joined someone else's profile, you earned absolutely nothing for your own. In a co-op game, that was a baffling design choice and made playing with friends feel more like a punishment than a reward. That said, I have to give the developers credit where it's due. Instead of abandoning the game or slowly trickling out fixes, they really buckled down and got to work. Over time they've addressed many of the biggest complaints, added a ton of quality-of-life improvements, and turned EverSiege: Untold Ages into a genuinely fun experience. It's refreshing to see a studio actually listen to its community and put in the effort to improve their game instead of just moving on to the next project. Is the game perfect? No. It still has room to grow, and its rough launch shouldn't be ignored. But if you can look past where it started and judge it by where it is now, I think you'll find a game that's improved tremendously and has a lot to offer. If you're looking for a cooperative, PvE-focused experience that borrows some of the best parts of MOBA gameplay without all the baggage, EverSiege: Untold Ages is definitely worth checking out. Especially on sale.

Overall, a positive experience. MOBA style time management and lane pushing, in a PvE game with co-op, and a difficulty curve that rewards players for pushing their team's limits. If playing against human MOBA players sounds less fun than a root canal, but you're bored of beating on brain-dead bots on other MOBA-likes, this may whet your team's appetite for a challenge. The higher levels will strain even elite players to defend the lane and still creep and hit bosses efficiently, as the day/night cycle and various elemental cataclysms shift the battlefield. "We have just seven days and six nights to defeat The Unraveler." You can, technically, clutch a win during the Eternal Night after day seven, but don't count on it outside of easy mode. The meta-progression system isn't very well thought out though. You gain a vital limited resource by beating higher difficultly levels for the first time, which is used to unlock the most important upgrades for build variety: Wargear upgrades. Wargears are the magical golem mecha the PCs use to fight, and fill the role of characters or champions in a MOBA. Upgrading them lets you select up to 3 extra perks in your load out screen, that will be automatically gained at levels 3, 6 and 9. When your character levels in-game, you get to pick one of just two perks, with very limited rerolls.* Gaining a second perk which is definitely one you need for your build is a huge power boost that is essential to higher difficultly levels. Whichever wargears you upgrade first are the ones you have to stick with to complete the remaining difficultly levels and level up the others. If you get stuck and want to change up your playstyle to break up the monotony, that's too bad. Once you do finally grind through the wall and upgrade you other characters, what are you supposed to do with them? You just beat the game. *Despite what some reviews say, these perks are always either for your current wargear, your elemental orb, generic perks any wargear can get, or an evolution for a skill you picked in your load out. You should NEVER get the option to choose an evolution perk for a skill you don't have equipped. This confusion may be caused be the Nature Orb having great skills, but it's passive having terrible nonsense evolutions. (Who is ever picking herb detection range over literally anything else?)

Updating my original positive review to negative as the first two hours of this game are very misleading - possibly by design. Your first couple of runs will be relaxing and largely easy - but as the game progresses you will be forced into increasingly artificially difficult experiences to the point at which I would say this game is LESS relaxing than playing Dota or League PvP (We're talking 2000+ enemy waves with 1700% bonus HP and damage). You are not given the tools to scale alongside the exponentially increasing enemies, and the only decent strategy I found to counter this was to essentially to a fully optimised 'full-clear' for 80 MINUTES STRAIGHT. If this sounds fun, they you'll probably love this - but for myself (and I NEVER thought I'd say this) I'd rather just play an actual MOBA.

The game is pretty much like eating unseasoned cold noodles. The issues with this game is that the matches are both too long (60-80 minutes) and not long enough. How? Well, for most of the match you are hitting like a wet noodle and falling over like a wet paper towel. Once you've got a build going, the match is all but over. What's more is the once you've played one "Age", you've pretty much played them all. The replayability just isn't there when the core gameplay is agonizingly dull for 90% of the game. Additionally, new abilities/heros/upgrades are locked behind harder and harder ages with no re-roll mechanic. And all of these are just a slightly different brand of flavourless noodles. Yikes. The matches also have you doing busy-work. Every in-game day you've got to run across the map collecting power nodes just so you can scale. This removes agency from the player as you're now forced to do this task over and over again. Often times you don't even have time to clear dungeons until you've massively out-scaled them due to the fact that they take too much time otherwise. To fix this issues, the devs would have to implement a pause function to the day/night cycle while inside a dungeon. What's more is the abilities each hero gets feel pretty uninspired and lacking in proper scaling. They don't scale with level and often have no utility outside of damage. Meaning unless you're pumping power nodes into the stats for those skills, you'll never use it after the early game. And I say "skills" as if there are multiple. But in reality there's 1 skill that scales with auto attacks, and 1 skill that scales with power nodes. So in reality you're scaling one skill on a cooldown at the cost of scaling auto attacks (which is by far the better choice for stat scaling). :/ The game concept is cool and sounds good on paper, but the execution leaves the game feeling "meh". Big thumbs down until the issues are addressed. For the devs: How to improve the game. -Allow remote or even automatic usage of power nodes and shrines after exploration. -Pause day/night time while inside dungeons and other instances. -Scale damaging aspect of abilities to level, and only the utility part to power nodes. -Make abilities hit much harder, they have a damn cooldown for a reason. Auto attacks shouldn't be the best damaging method, even when heavily invested. -Smoother scaling curve for heroes. Currently the balance is too heavily sided towards "late game". -On that note, give players a reason to play the eternal night. Currently you don't even seem to gain any additional resources for playing longer than needed. -Secondary abilities (the ones not tied to heroes) mostly feel underwhelming with a couple of exceptions. These abilities should have some "oumph!" to them. Decreasing the damage taken by allies that die instantly isn't exactly inspiring. Oh wow, they die in two volleys of the 10 catapults now instead of 1 volley. -Add the ability to respec points invested into heroes/abilities. And don't make it stupidly expensive, make it cheap to allow players to actually have some replay value of your game. I hate when games give players options to respec, but make it so expensive they may as well just start again or continue grinding. -Make larger or smaller maps that the player can choose. And possibly more varied zones. -What's more, the devs need to go back to each hero and make them unique. Right now they are just different flavours of the same hero. Dash ability 1. Auto attack scaling ability 2. AoE ability 3. There's no soul in these.

Eversiege scratches an itch I didn't know I had, which is doing PvE in a MOBA while also playing the economy side of an RTS. I ended up absolutely loving this game, and felt I should write a review because, after reading a lot of other reviews, I felt the game is getting a bad rap for kind of the wrong reasons. The game is indeed pretty difficult at first like a lot of the complaints say, but once it clicks and you understand the systems and builds and economy, it quickly settles down and you can beat every difficulty level on your first try right through to the end. To me, this means that the game's challenge level isn't due to tangible difficulty (like twitch skill, enemies being too strong, speed efficiency, etc), but due to onboarding and knowledge. You do start off each match pretty weak like a lot of reviews say, but I found that was only because I wasn't playing right. You're not supposed to wreck the waves or big jungle camps early on. You're supposed to fight weaker enemies and help the lane how you can in order to get stronger first. If there's a big jungle camp nearby harassing your lane and it seems impossible to deal with, you're not supposed to 1v1 it. You can do stuff like lure those big boys into your towers until they die, then you can get their big shards as a significant early match buff, repaying the extra time you spent luring and juking the big boys into your towers. There also used to be major multiplayer desync issues, which is where a lot of the negative reviews come from, but now they're mostly all gone after a few updates. The devs also clearly put a lot of work into a game that is only selling for $20 or $13 on sale. There is voice acting, there are old-school CGI cutscenes that introduce every enemy and boss type. Each age's map (even though it's the "same" square MOBA map where you're on the bottom and the enemy is on the top) changes pretty much every single asset contained within the map, from enemy camps and buff buildings, to boss lairs and dungeons -- even including how your creep lane twists and turns up to the enemy base. The game isn't without faults, though. Once you figure out an efficient build/upgrade order, you can pretty much ride it through every single difficulty. I started every match by building the Chronomancer's Council/Mage Tower combo to passively generate gold, and always rerolled away from the one specific boss that disables towers. There are multiple successful build/upgrade systems you can focus on, but you never need to switch it up from your preferred one. You also kind of do the same thing every match (even if lots of things change per match, like locations of everything -- bosses, available buffs, enemy factions, etc), but that can be said about a lot of match-based games. I think this game is super unique and had a blast all the way through. I've now spent a decent amount of time trying to find similar games to scratch this itch I didn't know I had, and haven't yet found one.

Contrary to what it might look like, game is unbearably repetitive. It's a festival of grind. Every mission is the same. Not enough time, constant pressure, and constant increase in difficulty. There is no sense of getting stronger. All missions are the same. You start with lvl 1, kill mobs (both main enemy and random trash around the map), pretend you're getting stronger only to have enemies got stronger with each passing night. Your units, even upgraded, can't stand their ground, so you constantlu have to help them, which pulls you away from exploring. Game pretends to be varied, just simply throwing more and more annoying obstacles, which suppusedly makes every run unique... That's just bullpoop. You don't get stronger with each run, you always do same things, and you have to deal with increasingly stronger enemies. There is only one map, and general pathing layout is always the same. Same for building. The only variable is what type of building there are. And always 3 mines, where two of them are ofc guarded by mid tiear enemies. Badly designed, poorly ballanced, with your troops being absolute trash, needing constant attention, and barely being able to stand against mobs. Spare yourself time and go somewhere else.
